summary: Reduce checkpoint capture and replay memory, and keep proof rollback journals on disk.

replay.detail: Mission-run and planning replay retain ordered claim IDs and decode one body at a time instead of retaining every body. Existing bounded base-replay pages remain unchanged. Projection ordering, per-claim quarantine and proof comparisons are unchanged; no replay is forced on upgrade.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes, triggers or schema-version change. Proof copies use a disk-backed rollback journal and temporary storage with a fixed 2 MiB page-cache target.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest change. Sealed envelope cuts and canonical ordering remain unchanged.

compatibility.detail: No wire or response-shape change. Checkpoint agreement and reader-equivalence contracts are unchanged. Metadata and bodies are captured from one consistent snapshot, including while another checkpoint trim commits.

downtime.detail: Requires the normal daemon binary restart. Restart-to-API and restart-to-health duration have not been measured for this change.

manual.detail: The checkpoint scratch directory needs disk space for both the database copy and its rollback journal. Capture pins a read snapshot until all retained bodies are decoded, so concurrent writes can grow the WAL during capture. No setting, identity migration or store repair is required.

recovery.detail: No on-disk migration. A binary rollback restores prior memory behavior. Proof scratch files are removed on completion or error.
